current_route.title: 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 alternating stack with independent thickness optimization on CaF2
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high/low index dielectric stack with 22 layers can produce two distinct transmission windows at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm through constructive interference, while adjacent bands experience destructive interference and suppression.
current_route.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating layers with optical thickness near λ/4 create high reflectance stopbands. By deviating from strict quarter-wave thicknesses and optimizing individually, multiple passbands can emerge at specific wavelengths where phase conditions allow transmission. The index contrast between ZnS and Al2O3 provides sufficient reflectance per interface to build effective stopbands with ~11 layer pairs.
